title: HarnessGateResult
description: Output written by Claude to .sessi-work/gate{N}_result.json after inline gate evaluation, then persisted to .methodology/gate{N}_result.json by finalize-gate (which patches composite_score / quality_complete / verdict / passed with its own computed values and syncs framework-owned dimension scores into breakdown). Round 21: this file was never loaded by any code, so it drifted into describing a shape no run has produced — required a per-dimension `passed` nothing writes, forbade the `null` scores CRG-only dimensions actually carry, and omitted the four fields every real breakdown entry does have. It is now validated at load time (core/quality_gate/gate_result_schema.py), which means it must keep describing reality: a mismatch is a bug in whichever side has moved, and both sides are now forced to say so. Round 26: `required` also has to describe what a PRODUCER is told to write. It listed open_critical_count / open_high_count, which no producer instruction has ever asked for — not the Gate 1 template in cli/fr_prompts/gate.py, not harness/ssi/prompts/evaluate_dimension.md, not the Gate 2/3/4 write steps in the phase workflows. The single fixture keeping this schema honest (taskq's gate4_result.json) happened to carry them, so validation agreed with reality by luck while obedient agents produced off-schema files: taskq-plus P3 blocked on malformed_gate_result at FR-01 and again at FR-04, passing 8 seconds later only because the retry volunteered fields nothing had requested. required now names only what a producer is instructed to write, and tests/test_gate_result_producer_parity.py holds every producer to it.

overall_score.description: Agent's own weighted composite. Null is normal and expected: finalize-gate recomputes the composite from breakdown weights and writes it to composite_score, so the agent has no reason to duplicate the arithmetic.

composite_score.description: Harness-computed weighted composite, patched in by finalize-gate on persist. Absent in the agent's own .sessi-work write.

meets_target.description: True when overall_score >= score_gate threshold. Null when the agent defers the verdict to the framework (the normal case — see overall_score).

quality_complete.description: True when meets_target AND open_critical_count==0 AND open_high_count==0. Advisory as written by the agent (HR-18): finalize-gate recomputes it and overwrites this field on persist.

verdict.description: PASS / FAIL, patched in by finalize-gate on persist.

passed.description: Top-level pass flag, patched in by finalize-gate on persist. NOTE: this is a gate-level field. There is no per-dimension `passed` — a dimension's outcome is score vs threshold.

open_critical_count.description: Number of unresolved critical severity issues. OPTIONAL and self-reported: no producer instruction asks for it, and absence reads as 0 (harness/harness_bridge.py's _first_non_null default). Kept readable rather than ignored because it is the one channel by which an evaluating agent can volunteer bad news — core/quality_gate/block_reason.py turns a non-zero value into an open_critical_findings block. The framework's own critical counts on the BLOCK paths do not come from here; finalize_gate constructs them from its own violation lists.

open_high_count.description: Number of unresolved high severity issues. Same contract as open_critical_count: optional, self-reported, absent means 0.

rounds_used.description: Evaluation rounds consumed reaching this result.

breakdown.description: Per-dimension score detail keyed by dimension name.

score.description: Null means the framework owns this dimension's score (CRG-only dimensions such as architecture) or no measurement applies (e.g. pytest-benchmark with no benchmarks). Readers MUST handle null explicitly — dict.get(k, default) does not substitute for a present null.

threshold.description: The dimension's pass bar. This is the field name — not `target`, which belongs to harness/ssi/scripts/score.py's separate .sessi-work/round_N/ output, and not `tool_score`, which no writer has ever produced.

tool_output.description: Path to the raw tool output backing this score.

tool_evidence.description: Quoted excerpt from the tool output that yields the score (checked by _check_tool_evidence).

tests_passed.description: Agent-counted pytest passes. Mandated as REQUIRED by the Gate 1 template (cli/fr_prompts/gate.py) and read by nothing: harness_bridge's _check_tests_failed / _check_test_skip_ratio re-derive both numbers by regex over tool_evidence, because a prose excerpt is harder to fabricate than an integer. Described here so it is documented rather than merely undeclared (see R26-DEFER-2).

tests_failed.description: Agent-counted pytest failures. Same contract as tests_passed — the blocking check parses `N failed` out of tool_evidence, not this field.

tests_skipped.description: Agent-counted pytest skips. Same contract as tests_passed — the skip-ratio WARN parses tool_evidence.

issues.description: Human-readable deficiencies found in this dimension.

findings.description: Structured findings, including framework enrichment (CRG hub nodes, large functions, dead code).

devil_advocate.description: Mirror of the top-level devil_advocate entry for this Tier 3 dimension.

da_waiver.description: Mirror of the top-level da_waiver entry. Requesting a waiver here does not grant one — see core/quality_gate/da_waiver.py.

framework_override.description: True when the framework, not the agent, supplied this dimension's score.

failing_dimensions.description: Names of dimensions that did not meet their individual thresholds.

devil_advocate.description: Per-Tier-3-dimension flag: was a Devil's Advocate challenge run?

da_waiver.description: Per-dimension score-threshold waiver REQUEST. Permission is checked against core.quality_gate.da_waiver.WAIVABLE_DIMENSIONS at collection; necessity is adjudicated in finalize_gate against the framework's own score.

devil_advocate_evidence.description: Per-dimension challenge + response prose. The harness checks presence and length, not truth — it is a documentation artifact, not a correctness guarantee.

enforcer_sha.description: Harness commit that produced this verdict (Round 19 站3), with a -dirty suffix when the working tree was not clean.

gate_num.description: Gate number this result belongs to. Provenance only — no consumer reads it from the file; every code path already knows its gate from GateContext. Gate 2/3/4 results spell it this way.

gate.description: Gate 1's spelling of gate_num — cli/fr_prompts/gate.py's template emits `"gate": 1`. Two names for one provenance field, neither read from the file; documented rather than silently undescribed (see docs/PROPOSAL_ADJUDICATIONS.md R26-DEFER-1 for the unification).

fr_id.description: Functional requirement ID if gate is FR-scoped.
